subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the equation of the straight line parallel to the line 3x+4y=7 and passing through the point of intersection of the lines x−2y−3=0 and x+3y−6=0.

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.62 — SAQ chapter 9 The Straight Line, answer 56.1. Printed appearance: TS 16. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed against this answer. It is not a bare guess: the SAME CHAPTER prints 1+1+2 on answer 59 (book p.63), and this answer is cut to the same shape — the two setting-up moves at one mark each and the closing work at two. Where an answer's own shape is four equal moves instead, 1+1+1+1 is used and this note says so. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. NOTE: The Straight Line is the FIRST Maths-1B unit to occupy ALL THREE sections of the paper — the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.3) gives it 2+2 marks in Section A, 4 in Section B and 7 in Section C, 15 in all, tying Differentiation as the highest-scoring unit on the paper. It therefore has three separate chapters in this book: LAQ chapter 1 (book pp.14-18), SAQ chapter 9 (pp.61-64) and VSAQ chapter 14 (pp.79-82). All three boundaries were walked: p.19 opens Pair of Straight Lines, p.65 opens Limits & Continuity, and p.83 opens 3-D Coordinates. The book's separate STAR QUESTIONS PLUS bank (pp.104-108) contributes three more, answers 182-184, authored here as sqp1-sqp3. RE-CUT 2026-08-31: this card was filed as SAQ at 4 marks and is now VSAQ at 2 marks. The original label came from the Baby Bullet-Q blueprint for the superseded 75-mark paper; the Sri Chaitanya FAST TRACK IPE Mathematics-IB 2026-27 edition files this chapter under the banner 8M + 2 × 2M = 12M, asks this question as Very Short Answer Question 37, and prints no short-answer block for it at all. Only the question was taken; the working, the mark split and every note here are ours (docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md). The mathematics and the steps are unchanged; only the mark scheme moved — the four marks become two, at 0 + 1 + 0 + 1: the mark for method sits on solving the pair for the point, which is the only real algebra here, and the mark for the answer on the finished line. Reading the parallel slope off the coefficients and quoting the point-slope form are carried unmarked as setup. Still unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Find the required slope
steps.margin_note: The new line is parallel to a given line, so its slope is fixed before any point is known. Read the given slope off the coefficients as −a/b, and use the same value.
lines: A parallel line has the SAME slope, so the required slope is −3/4

recall.must_convey: That the slope of the given line is found as −a/b and the required slope is the same, because the lines are parallel.

steps.why: Slope comes first because it needs only the OTHER line, not the point — and the point takes more work.
common_mistakes: Taking the negative reciprocal when the lines are parallel.
steps.memory_tip: PARALLEL means the same slope, fixed before any point is known. Read it off as −a/b.

steps.label: Solve for the point
steps.margin_note: First mark. The new line passes through the meeting point of two OTHER lines, so solve that pair. This half is independent of the slope work above.

recall.must_convey: That the two lines are solved together to find the point the required line passes through.

steps.why: The question gives the line's direction one way and its position another, and the two are found independently before being combined.
common_mistakes: Solving the wrong pair of lines.
steps.memory_tip: Solve the OTHER pair of lines for the point. This half is independent of the slope work.

steps.label: Write the point-slope form
steps.margin_note: With a point and a slope, the point-slope form y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) writes the line in one line.

steps.why: A point and a slope determine a line uniquely, which is why the two independent halves are enough between them.

steps.margin_note: Last mark. Clear the fractions and collect into ax + by + c = 0 form.

insider_note: The slope is available before the point is, so read −3/4 off the given line first. Parallel keeps that slope unchanged, and the final line divides through by 5 to reach 3x + 4y − 15 = 0.
